subject: Quantitative Aptitude
topic: Simple and Compound Interest — Advanced Problems (W11 B1)

questions.stem: Find the Simple Interest on ₹5,000 at 8% per annum for 3 years. What is the total amount at the end of 3 years?
Find the Compound Interest on ₹2,000 at 10% per annum for 2 years, compounded annually.
questions.explanation: C is correct. A = P(1+R/100)ⁿ = 2000×(1.1)² = 2000×1.21 = ₹2,420. CI = 2420−2000 = ₹420. Alternatively: Year 1 interest = 200. Year 2 interest = (2000+200)×10% = 220. Total CI = 200+220 = ₹420. Trap: ₹400 = SI for 2 years (2000×10×2/100); ₹380 = wrong; ₹440 = 10% of 2200×2 (double-counting).

questions.stem: What is the difference between Compound Interest and Simple Interest on ₹10,000 at 10% per annum for 2 years?
If the Simple Interest on a principal of ₹1,500 for 4 years is ₹480, what is the annual rate of interest?
Find the principal if the Simple Interest at 7% per annum for 3 years is ₹630.
Find the Compound Interest on ₹8,000 at 10% per annum for 1 year, compounded half-yearly.
questions.explanation: B is correct. Half-yearly rate = 10/2 = 5%. Number of periods = 2. A = 8000×(1.05)² = 8000×1.1025 = ₹8,820. CI = 8820−8000 = ₹820. Trap: ₹800 = SI for 1 year (8000×10×1/100); ₹840 = wrong computation; ₹850 = 8000×10.625% (wrong).

questions.stem: In how many years will a sum of money double itself at 8% Simple Interest per annum?
questions.explanation: C is correct. For money to double: SI = P. P×R×T/100 = P → T = 100/R = 100/8 = 12.5 years. Shortcut: years to double at SI = 100/R%. Verify: SI = P×8×12.5/100 = P ✓ → Amount = 2P. Trap: 10 years → only if R=10%; 12 years → R=8.33%.

questions.stem: Two principal amounts are in ratio 2:3. Both are invested at 10% per annum Simple Interest for 2 years. If the interest on the smaller principal is ₹400, what is the interest on the larger?
questions.explanation: C is correct. Smaller P: SI = P×10×2/100 = P/5 = ₹400 → P = ₹2,000. Ratio 2:3, so larger P = 3000. SI on larger = 3000×10×2/100 = ₹600. Alternatively: since rate and time are same, SI is directly proportional to P. SI ratio = P ratio = 2:3. Larger SI = (3/2)×400 = ₹600. Trap: ₹500 = (5/4)×400 (uses wrong ratio 4:5); ₹550 = ₹400+₹150 (wrong addition).

questions.stem: Find the Compound Interest on ₹2,000 at 10% per annum for 3 years, compounded annually.
A bank offers 10% per annum compounded half-yearly. What is the effective annual rate of interest (approximately)?
questions.explanation: B is correct. Half-yearly rate = 5%. For ₹100: A after 1 year = 100×(1.05)² = 100×1.1025 = ₹110.25. Effective CI = ₹10.25 = 10.25% on ₹100. This is higher than the nominal 10% because of the compounding within the year. Formula: effective annual rate = (1+r/n)ⁿ−1 = (1+0.10/2)²−1 = 1.1025−1 = 10.25%. Trap: 10.00% = nominal rate (no compounding benefit); 10.50% = overestimates; 11.00% = quarterly compounding approximation.
